audience: New Finance users and administrators who must review the Accounting settings before the Accounting module goes live.
goal: Walk through **Configuration › Settings › Accounting** section by section and understand what each setting controls: **taxes, currencies, customer invoices and payments, vendor bills and payments, default accounts, bank import, fiscal periods, analytics and reporting**. Nothing is changed. It is a review of what the company has configured.
before: You can open the **Accounting** app and its **Configuration** menu. Settings are visible to Accounting administrators.
Agree any change with the **Finance Manager** and the ERP team first. These settings apply to the **whole company**.
outcome: You have seen every Accounting setting block that must be reviewed before go-live, and what each one decides.
You know which settings are fixed at go-live (localisation, main currency) and which can change later.
You know that nothing is stored until **Save** is pressed.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The red banner at the top ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases. The values shown (VAT 18%, fiscal year ending 31 March, and so on) belong to that database and will differ from yours.
This tour is **read-only**. The automated run scrolls to each setting and outlines it. It does not tick, type or choose anything, and it never presses **Save**.

Several fields are empty in the test data: the **Package** under Fiscal Localization, the exchange-difference **Gain** and **Loss** accounts, the bank suspense and outstanding accounts, and the deferred expense and revenue accounts. On a live company these must be filled in.
The settings page is long. The left panel lists every app; **Accounting** is highlighted, and everything on the right belongs to the Finance module.

phases.title: Open the Accounting settings
phases.summary: Go from the Accounting app to Configuration › Settings.
phases.checkpoint: The **Settings** page is open on the **Accounting** tab.

phases.title: Localisation and taxes
phases.summary: Fiscal localisation, default taxes, tax return periodicity and rounding.
phases.checkpoint: You know the fixed foundations: localisation package, default taxes, return schedule and rounding rule.

phases.title: Currencies
phases.summary: The company currency and automatic exchange rates.
phases.checkpoint: You know the company currency and how exchange rates are updated.

phases.title: Customer invoices and payments
phases.summary: How invoices are sent, their terms, credit limits, and how customers pay.
phases.checkpoint: You know how invoices leave Odoo and how payments come in.

phases.title: Vendor bills and payments
phases.summary: Purchase receipts, bill prediction and cheques.
phases.checkpoint: You know how vendor bills are recorded and how vendors are paid.

phases.title: Default accounts and bank
phases.summary: Exchange difference, bank suspense, deferred entries and statement import.
phases.checkpoint: You know which accounts Odoo posts to automatically, and which bank formats you can import.

phases.title: Periods, analytics and reporting
phases.summary: Fiscal year, analytic accounting and report options.
phases.checkpoint: You know the fiscal year end and the optional analytic and reporting features.

phases.title: Save
phases.checkpoint: You know that changes are stored only when you press **Save**.

glossary.meaning: The country package that installs the chart of accounts, taxes, fiscal positions and legal statements. Set once at implementation.
The sales and purchase tax used when a product has no tax of its own.
How tax is rounded: on every invoice line, or once on the invoice total.
The company currency. Every ledger balance and report is expressed in it.
The gain or loss that arises when a foreign-currency invoice is paid at a different rate from the one it was booked at.
Holds a bank statement line until it is matched with an invoice or payment.
Money registered in Odoo that has not yet cleared the bank.
Entries that spread income or cost over several periods, such as insurance or subscriptions.
A second, management view of cost and revenue by project, department or machine.

1.title: Open the Accounting app
1.do: On the Odoo home screen, click the **Accounting** app.
actions: Go to the Odoo home screen.
1.see: The Accounting app opens with its menu bar across the top.
1.why: The Finance settings are reached from the Accounting app.

2.title: Find the Configuration menu
2.do: Look along the top menu bar for **Configuration**.
actions: If **Configuration** is hidden, click the **+** at the end of the bar to reveal it.
2.why: Not every menu fits on a narrow screen, so the last entries can hide behind a **+**.
2.tip: A wider browser window shows the whole menu without the **+**.

3.title: Open Configuration › Settings
actions: Wait for the page to load.
3.see: The **Settings** page, with a list of apps on the left and the settings on the right.
3.why: This one page controls how the whole Finance module behaves: taxes, currencies, invoicing, payments, default accounts, period locks and reporting.

4.title: Check you are on the Accounting tab
4.do: Check that **Accounting** is highlighted in the left panel.
4.see: **Accounting** is highlighted, so everything on the right belongs to the Finance module.
4.why: The page lists settings for every app. Work down the Accounting sections in order.

5.title: Fiscal Localization
5.do: Find **Fiscal Localization** at the top of the Accounting settings.
actions: Find the **Fiscal Localization** block (outlined in red).
5.see: The country package that supplies the taxes, fiscal positions, chart of accounts and legal statements. In the test data the **Package** field is blank.
5.why: This is the foundation of the module. It is set once at implementation.
5.warning: Do **not** change the localisation package once journal entries exist.

6.title: Default Taxes
6.do: Find **Default Taxes** and read the **Sales Tax** and **Purchase Tax**.
6.see: The default taxes applied when a product carries none. In the test data both are **VAT 18%**.
6.why: Default taxes are applied automatically when a product has no tax of its own.
6.tip: Fix the default taxes before you create any invoice or bill.

7.title: Tax Return Periodicity
7.do: Find **Tax Return Periodicity** and read the schedule.
7.where: Settings > Accounting > Taxes > Tax Return Periodicity
7.see: How often the tax return is filed (**monthly**), the reminder (**7 days after period**), and the journal for the tax closing entry (**TAX JOURNAL**).
7.why: Odoo uses this to schedule the tax return reminder and to post the closing entry.
7.tip: The **Configure your tax accounts** link sets the tax payable and receivable accounts.

8.title: Rounding Method
8.do: Find **Rounding Method** and see which option is chosen.
actions: Read which option is selected: **Round per Line** or **Round Globally**.
8.see: **Round Globally** is selected in the test data.
8.why: It decides how the tax total is computed. *Round per Line* rounds tax on every invoice line; *Round Globally* rounds once on the invoice total.
8.warning: Changing this later changes the totals on new documents. Agree it with the tax team first.

9.title: Main Currency
9.see: The company currency (**LKR** in the test data).
9.why: Every ledger balance and report is expressed in this currency. Foreign-currency invoices are converted to it using the rate on the document date.
9.warning: It is fixed at go-live and cannot be changed once entries are posted.

10.title: Automatic Currency Rates
10.where: Settings > Accounting > Currencies > Automatic Currency Rates
10.see: It is switched on, with the service **European Central Bank** and the interval **Manually**.
10.why: If you trade in foreign currency, Odoo can refresh exchange rates by itself instead of someone keying them in every morning.
10.tip: Set the **Interval** to daily, weekly or monthly for rates to update on their own.

11.title: Default Sending Options
11.do: Find **Default Sending Options** under Customer Invoices.
11.where: Settings > Accounting > Customer Invoices > Default Sending Options
11.see: **Download** and **Send Email** are ticked; **Peppol format** and **Send by Post** are not.
11.why: These options are pre-selected on every invoice when you click **Send & Print**, so set them to the way Finance actually sends documents.

12.title: Default Terms & Conditions
12.where: Settings > Accounting > Customer Invoices > Default Terms & Conditions
actions: Read whether it is **Add a Note** or **Add a link to a Web Page**.
12.see: It is switched on, with **Add a link to a Web Page** chosen. **Update Terms** and **Preview** are links below.
12.why: Your standard terms are printed at the bottom of every invoice, sales order and quotation.
12.tip: Use **Update Terms** to edit the wording.

13.title: Sales Credit Limit
13.where: Settings > Accounting > Customer Invoices > Sales Credit Limit
13.see: It is switched on, with a **Default Credit Limit** of 0.0000 in the test data.
13.why: Odoo warns users when a customer's total receivable goes past the limit.
13.warning: A limit of **0** means no limit is checked. Set a value greater than zero to activate the check. Individual limits can then be set on each customer.

14.title: Customer Payments
actions: Read the four options under it.
points: **Invoice Online Payment** lets customers pay from the invoice portal (ticked in the test data).
**Batch Payments** groups several receipts into one deposit, which eases bank reconciliation.
**SEPA Direct Debit** collects payments in one click.
**QR Codes** prints a scannable payment code on the invoice.
14.see: The Customer Payments options, with only **Invoice Online Payment** ticked.
14.why: These options control how money comes in.

15.title: Purchase Receipt and digitisation
15.where: Settings > Accounting > Vendor Bills > Purchase Receipt
actions: Look at **Predict vendor bill product** beside it.
15.see: Both are ticked in the test data.
15.why: A **Purchase Receipt** records an over-the-counter purchase without a formal vendor bill. **Predict vendor bill product** makes Odoo suggest the product on bill lines from what you bought before, which speeds up data entry.

16.title: Vendor Payments: Checks
actions: Read **Check Layout**, **Multi-Pages Check Stub** and the margins.
16.see: **Checks** is ticked, with **Check Layout: None** and margins of 0.25.
16.why: It enables paying vendors by cheque and sets the printing options.
16.warning: Cheques here are printed by a custom module, so the standard **Check Layout** is deliberately left as **None**. Do not change it without checking with the ERP team.

17.title: Exchange difference accounts
17.where: Settings > Accounting > Default Accounts > Exchange difference
actions: Find the **Post Exchange difference entries in** block.
17.see: The journal **Exchange Difference**. **Gain** and **Loss** are empty in the test data.
17.why: When a foreign-currency invoice is paid at a different rate, Odoo posts the difference automatically using these settings.
17.warning: If these are wrong or empty, foreign-currency settlements land in the wrong profit-and-loss line.

18.title: Bank suspense and outstanding accounts
18.do: Find **Post bank transactions and payments in**.
18.where: Settings > Accounting > Default Accounts > Post bank transactions and payments in
points: **Bank Suspense** holds a statement line until it is matched.
**Outstanding Receipts** and **Outstanding Payments** hold money registered in Odoo that has not yet cleared the bank.
**Internal Transfer** is used when moving money between your own bank and cash accounts.
18.see: The four accounts that drive bank reconciliation.
18.why: Bank reconciliation does not work correctly unless these are set.

19.title: Deferred entries
19.where: Settings > Accounting > Default Accounts > Post Deferred entries in
actions: Find the **Post Deferred entries in** block.
Read the journal and the accounts.
points: **Journal**, **Deferred Expense** and **Deferred Revenue** are the journal and accounts used.
**Generate Expense / Revenue Entries** decides whether entries are made on invoice validation or manually.
**Amount Computation** is the basis for spreading the amount (months in the test data).
19.see: The deferred-entries settings. The journal is **O/B**; the accounts are empty in the test data.
19.why: Used when income or cost must be spread over several periods: service contracts, insurance, subscriptions.

20.title: Bank statement import formats
20.do: Find the import formats under **Bank & Cash**.
actions: Read which import formats are ticked.
20.see: **CSV, XLS and XLSX Import**, **OFX Import** and **CAMT Import** are ticked; **QIF Import** is not.
20.why: Tick the file formats your banks provide so statements can be imported instead of typed.
20.tip: **Anglo-Saxon Accounting**, just below, decides whether the cost of goods sold is booked at delivery. That is a stock-valuation decision, not an import setting.

21.title: Fiscal Year
21.where: Settings > Accounting > Fiscal Periods > Fiscal Year
21.see: The last day of the financial year: **31 March** in the test data.
21.tip: **Fiscal Years** lets you define a year longer or shorter than twelve months, and the **Invoicing Switch Threshold** ignores invoices dated before a chosen date.

22.title: Analytics
actions: Look at **Budget Management** and **Margin Analysis** beside and below it.
22.see: All three are ticked in the test data.
22.why: Analytic accounting adds a second, management view of cost and revenue by department, project or machine. **Budget Management** compares actuals against expected revenue and cost. **Margin Analysis** shows margin on sales.

23.title: Add totals below sections
23.do: Find **Add totals below sections** under Reporting.
23.where: Settings > Accounting > Reporting > Add totals below sections
actions: Find the **Add totals below sections** block.
23.see: It is not ticked in the test data.
23.why: When ticked, a subtotal is printed under each section of the financial reports, so the Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss read the way accountants expect.
23.tip: **Storno Accounting**, below it, reverses entries with negative amounts instead of swapping debit and credit.

24.title: Save your changes
24.do: Find **Save** at the top left. Press it only if you changed a setting.
actions: Look at the top left of the page.
**Save** stores your changes; **Discard** throws them away.
24.why: Nothing you have looked at is stored until you press **Save**.
24.warning: Settings apply to the whole company. Agree any change with the Finance Manager and the ERP team before you save. The automated test only points at **Save** and never presses it.
24.tip: That completes the tour: you have reviewed every required Accounting setting.
